NAS (Synology, QNAP…), Windows PC with a shared folder, or Samba server. Games must be sorted into one folder per console.

Emulators marked “folder to allow” need access to the console folder: in their settings, add the folder shown (server cache) and, for your local games, the console folder on the TV or USB drive.

Two kinds of sources. A folder on the TV or a USB drive: games are launched in place. A home server (NAS or PC, SMB share): the game is copied to the TV when launched, then kept in cache.
No controller · pair the Xbox Nano
Put games in one folder per console at the root of the source: snes, megadrive, psx, ps2, gc, n64, gba, dreamcast, psp…
Without it, the app can’t read games from the TV or USB drives, or copy games from the server.
%1$s can’t start a game whose folder contains an apostrophe. Rename the folder.
Screen not available on this TV: see Settings for the adb command.
Connection problem with %1$s, trying again (%2$d of %3$d)…
This game’s source was removed. Run “Refresh”.
Server games are copied here before they start. The oldest are deleted when the limit is reached. Your saves stay in the emulators.
Permission refused. To show the battery, allow “Nearby devices” for RetroSalon in the TV settings: Apps → RetroSalon → Permissions.
If your controller uses Bluetooth, like the Xbox Nano, RetroSalon needs the “Nearby devices” permission to show its battery. It is only used to read the controller’s battery level.
Screen not available on this TV. In the TV settings, go to Apps → RetroSalon → Permissions.
1. On the TV: Settings → Remotes & Accessories → Pair accessory.
2. Turn on the controller (Xbox button), then hold the pair button until the logo flashes fast.
3. Choose “Xbox Wireless Controller”. RetroArch, PPSSPP, Dolphin and most emulators map it automatically.
Choose the emulator for each console and see what is left to set up.

Consoles that use RetroArch start with the RetroArch built into RetroSalon: nothing to install. During a game, open RetroArch’s menu with Back on the remote, or Menu + View (Start + Select) on the controller.

Android runs in 32-bit on this TV. Some emulators only exist in 64-bit and can’t be installed here: Dolphin (GameCube, Wii), Azahar (3DS), NetherSX2 and ARMSX2 (PS2), Eden (Switch) and the 2024 version of MAME4droid. The other emulators work.
Android runs in 64-bit on this TV: every emulator RetroSalon supports can be installed, as long as the TV’s Android version and power are enough.

Android runs in 64-bit on this TV, but can’t run 64-bit ARM apps. NetherSX2, ARMSX2 and the 2024 version of MAME4droid only exist for ARM and can’t be installed here; for Eden, take its ChromeOS version. The other emulators can be installed, as long as the TV’s Android version and power are enough.
You can find this again in Settings → Emulators.

RetroArch is built into RetroSalon, with its cores: nothing to install. For the PlayStation: the built-in PCSX ReARMed and SwanStation cores, DuckStation or ePSXe. For MAME4droid: version 0.139u1, which needs games in the MAME 0.139 format.
With an x86 processor, take the x86 version of each emulator when there is one.
On the next screen, turn on RetroSalon, then come back with the Back button.
Android will ask you to confirm: choose “Allow”.
One app to launch games from all your consoles, with the Xbox Nano controller or the remote.
File access: to read your games on the TV or a USB drive, and copy games from the server into the cache. RetroSalon only browses the folders you add as a source.
